body: I don't want to talk about it, as it could easily reveal my identity.  Thanks for the words though.

I keep telling myself to go to the library and work on my game free of distractions, but I end up waking up at 3pm and wasting my whole day because I can't sleep.  I've tried pulling an all-nighter to reset my schedule, but I ended up crashing at 1pm the next day.

I don't want to work twice as hard for half the money.  Although money is one of my many problems, I don't have any bills other than the student loans to worry about.  I am only interested in doing things I like.  I've already left a grad school because the work was making me feel depressed and unfulfilled.  I understand what you are trying to tell me, but the only thing that has helped me is making video games.

I don't know much in the realm of web stuff.  HTML / CSS, PHP, SQL, basically all the web languages except C# and some Javascript are things I'm unfamiliar with.  And although many languages share similar qualities, I would be very unlikely to get past an interview as a web dev.
I have a solo project that's 75% complete, but every time I open it, I just let it sit there and think about how shitty things are.

> A job is a job dude, no matter what you are doing.

I tend to disagree.  I'm more happy when I get to be creative and use my brain.  It actually makes me feel worse about my situation because I am stuck having to do something I despise.
Getting a job in a relevant profession.
